sample.name: One engine, read through the day
sample.what: The library brain, layered: one day instead of one stay. Pick a time of day or play it, and watch the records flow in and the engine’s answers fill by the 6 PM freeze.

text: Here is the build, in the order it happens.
bullets: First, read access. Your IT team links the systems that already hold admissions, discharges, inpatient notes and billing. We write nothing back.
Second, discharge. The bed plan runs on discharge times, so discharge is built and linked before the bed mapping.
Then one engine does five jobs. It maps tomorrow’s beds and ICU beds, checks discharge times, holds emergency beds back and sets call-in times.
chat.invite: Pick any part to see what it reads and what it makes. Or tell me which systems your hospital runs.
chat.note: Read access and discharge first. The engine comes after.
prompts: What exactly would our IT team do?
Why must discharge be built first?
What if some records are on paper?

blocks.condition: The 2 PM pass is a first picture. Only the 6 PM freeze sends call-in times out.

sheets.title: OPD advice comes in
sheets.text: Each advice to admit is read as it is written, with the procedure and the date. The emergency trend is read from your past admissions.
sheets.entry: How many planned admissions do you have on a usual day?

sheets.title: ICU signals due
sheets.text: ICU patients need their step-down signal by 1 PM. The engine adds patients near the usual ICU stay for their procedure.
sheets.entry: Who gives the step-down signal in your ICU?

sheets.title: First mapping pass
sheets.text: Tomorrow’s planned admissions are set against empty beds and beds likely to free up. The teams are told what to confirm.

lines.label: Tells
lines.value: The discharge team and Medical Supervisory

sheets.entry: Who should hear about the 2 PM pass first?

sheets.title: Rounds confirm
sheets.text: On the evening round each predicted date is confirmed or corrected. The engine takes in every answer.
sheets.entry: At what time do your evening rounds end?

hand.does: Confirms or corrects each predicted date.

sheets.title: Final freeze
sheets.text: Tomorrow’s plan is frozen. Each patient coming in has one bed and a call-in time. What is still unmapped is shared with everyone.

lines.label: Also makes
lines.value: The list still without a bed

hand.does: Checks the freeze before the call-in times go out.

blocks.label: Your IT team’s part
blocks.sub: About two weeks. We read the records you already hold, and we write nothing back.
